newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN POLICE STAGE NATION-WIDE CHILD PORN RAID.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN POLICE STAGE NATION-WIDE CHILD PORN RAID.

text.p: Police searching for paedophile pornography and child porn networks raided 60 homes and other establishments around Belgium in a coordinated operation on Thursday.
"Based on a list of addresses we received from France and another from Britain we carried out searches at 60 or so places today," Brussels court spokesman Josef Colpin told Reuters.
He said about 20 of the searches were at addresses in and around Brussels, with the rest scattered throughout the country.
Colpin declined to give details of what, if any, material had been seized or if arrests had been made. Belgian television said later police took away videos and documents.

Belgium has been in turmoil since mid-August when convicted rapist Marc Dutroux was arrested. Two sexually-abused young girls were rescued from a dungeon in one of his houses and police subsequently discovered the buried bodies of four more.
Eight-year-olds Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo had been missing since June 1995. Dutroux said they starved to death early last year.
Their bodies were found next to that of a former Dutroux accomplice, Frenchman Bernard Weinstein, on another property belonging to Dutroux elsewhere in the central city of Charleroi.
Dutroux, who was released on parole in 1992 after serving three years of a 13-year sentence for multiple child rape, has admitted murdering Weinstein.
The bodies of teenagers An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks, missing for a year, were unearthed in early September at another property in Charleroi connected with Dutroux.
Last October more than 250,000 people marched through Brussels in a demonstration of support for victims of the paedophile ring and of public disgust at the whole legal and political system.
Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene immediately promised wide-ranging reforms, and parents of the children met him for three hours on Thursday evening to review progress.

"(We have) undertaken that the government will do everything...The four projects that correspond to the parents' concerns will be voted through before parliament goes on holiday (in summer)," Dehaene told reporters after the meeting.

These included giving more prominence to victims of crime, as well as reviewing the magistrate system and the execution of sentences. Work would also be done on setting up a private centre to deal with cases of missing children.
Parents and relatives of the dead girls told Belgian television afterwards they were satisfied with the meeting.
A special parliamentary commission is investigating the handling of the past searches for the dead girls.
Its chairman, Marc Verwilghen, said earlier this week it was obvious that, had it not been for bungling by police and magistrates, the girls would be alive today.
There have been allegations Dutroux's gang was only able to operate so long -- even though he was under secret surveillance by gendarmes -- because Dutroux had high-level protection.

Police on Thursday ended a fruitless three-week underground search at an abandoned coal mining complex in Charleroi, where they have been looking for signs of several other missing children, including bodies.
Searches will continue next week above ground at the site.
